title: Bhikkhus, just as a skilled carpenter or his apprentice uses a small peg to knock out, drive out, and remove a larger peg; so too,…
content: Bhikkhus, just as a skilled carpenter or his apprentice uses a small peg to knock out, drive out, and remove a larger peg; so too, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu, by attending to a certain sign, gives rise to evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion, then that bhikkhu should attend to another sign connected with what is wholesome, different from that sign. By attending to another sign connected with what is wholesome, those evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion are abandoned and subside. Through their abandonment, his mind becomes inwardly steady, settled, unified, and concentrated.

title: Bhikkhus, as long as a teacher lives over-attached to material things, being an heir to material things, and lives in connection with material things, this…
content: Bhikkhus, as long as a teacher lives over-attached to material things, being an heir to material things, and lives in connection with material things, this bargain does not occur: 'We will do this thus, and thus we will not do that.' How much more so for the Tathāgata, bhikkhus, who lives completely unconnected with material things.

title: Bhikkhus, these four things are few, easily obtained, and blameless. What four? Among robes, the dust-heap rag is few, easily obtained, and blameless. Among foods,…
content:
Bhikkhus, these four things are few, easily obtained, and blameless. What four? Among robes, the dust-heap rag is few, easily obtained, and blameless. Among foods, the lump of almsfood is few, easily obtained, and blameless. Among lodgings, the foot of a tree is few, easily obtained, and blameless. Among medicines, fermented cow's urine is few, easily obtained, and blameless. These four things are few, easily obtained, and blameless. Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is content with these few, easily obtained things, I declare that this is a factor of asceticism for him.

Content with things that are few,
Easily obtained, and blameless,
Mind not disturbed
Regarding lodgings, robes, food and drink.
Not worried about the direction one should go,
The Dhamma proclaimed, conducive to asceticism,
He possesses them fully,
For a bhikkhu who knows contentment, who is not heedless.

title: There are these six things that are part of true knowledge. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception…
content: There are these six things that are part of true knowledge. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of non-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. These six things, bhikkhus, are part of true knowledge.

title: Bhikkhus, as long as beings have not directly known as it actually is, regarding these four elements, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger,…
content:
Bhikkhus, as long as beings have not directly known as it actually is, regarding these four elements, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, the escape as escape, they do not live with a mind of seclusion, unattached, unrelated, abandoning obstacles, in relation to the heavenly world, the Māra world, the Brahmā world, together with the generations of samaṇas and brahmins, devas and humans.

And, bhikkhus, when beings have directly known as it actually is, regarding these four elements, the gratification as gratification, the danger as danger, the escape as escape, they live with a mind of seclusion, unattached, unrelated, abandoning obstacles, in relation to the heavenly world, the Māra world, the Brahmā world, together with the generations of samaṇas and brahmins, devas and humans.

title: Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are deceitful, stubborn, talkative, fraudulent, haughty, and unconcentrated — those bhikkhus are not my bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus have fallen away from…
content: Those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are deceitful, stubborn, talkative, fraudulent, haughty, and unconcentrated — those bhikkhus are not my bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus have fallen away from this Dhamma and Discipline. And they do not achieve growth, increase, or expansion in this Dhamma and Discipline. And those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, who are not deceitful, not talkative, wise, not stubborn, well-concentrated — those bhikkhus are indeed my bhikkhus. Those bhikkhus have not fallen away from this Dhamma and Discipline, and they achieve growth, increase, and expansion in this Dhamma and Discipline.

title: Bhikkhus, there are these three taints. What three? The taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance. Bhikkhus, these are…
content:
Bhikkhus, there are these three taints. What three? The taint of sensual desire, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance. Bhikkhus, these are the three taints.

One who has abandoned the taint of sensual desire,
And the taint of ignorance,
Who has destroyed the taint of existence,
Is liberated from all attachments.
Bearing his final body,
He has conquered Māra and his host.

title: ( Blessed One ): For one without anger, Whence does anger come? Living tamed, with right livelihood, Liberated, through right knowledge. That one lives thus,…
content:
( Blessed One ):
For one without anger,
Whence does anger come?
Living tamed, with right livelihood,
Liberated, through right knowledge.
That one lives thus,
A life of peace.
Those who, when reviled,
Revile in return,
Do evil to themselves,
And also evil to others.
Those who, when reviled,
Do not revile in return,
That person wins a battle,
A victory for both self and other.
That one seeks the benefit
Of both self and other.
And the one who reviled,
Understanding, calms down.
A physician to both,
Healing self and healing other,
People think him a fool,
Because they do not understand the Dhamma.

title: Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects: 'If someone were to break up my friends by divisive speech, that would be undesirable and unpleasing for me.…
content: Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects: 'If someone were to break up my friends by divisive speech, that would be undesirable and unpleasing for me. But if I were to break up another's friends by divisive speech, that would be undesirable and unpleasing for that person. This state that is undesirable and unpleasing for me is also undesirable and unpleasing for others. Since this state is undesirable and unpleasing for me, why should I impose it on others?' Reflecting thus, he himself abstains from divisive speech, encourages others to abstain from divisive speech, and speaks in praise of abstaining from divisive speech. Thus, in verbal conduct, he becomes completely pure.

title: 'A transgression has overcome me, Venerable Sir, foolish, deluded, and unwholesome as I am. For while the Blessed One was teaching the bhikkhus a Dhamma…
content: 'A transgression has overcome me, Venerable Sir, foolish, deluded, and unwholesome as I am. For while the Blessed One was teaching the bhikkhus a Dhamma talk connected with the training, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, I felt impatient and displeased, thinking: 'This samaṇa is too meticulous.' Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One accept my transgression as a transgression, so that I may restrain myself in the future.' - 'Indeed, Kassapogotta, a transgression has overcome you, foolish, deluded, and unwholesome as you are. For while I was teaching the bhikkhus a Dhamma talk connected with the training, encouraging, inspiring, and gladdening them, you felt impatient and displeased, thinking: 'This samaṇa is too meticulous.' And, Kassapogotta, since you see your transgression as a transgression and make amends according to the Dhamma, I accept your confession. This is growth in the Noble One's Discipline, that one sees a transgression as a transgression, makes amends according to the Dhamma, and restrains oneself in the future.'
